RESEARCH PROFILE

A researcher's route into applied AI

Amal is a Ph.D. Research Scholar in Commerce & International Business at the Central University of Kerala, where his doctoral work sits at the intersection of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and digital marketing analytics. His research applies supervised and unsupervised learning to a deceptively hard question: what actually predicts customer conversion in a digital marketing campaign?

That work has now moved from conference floor to peer review — with two Scopus Q1 journal articles published in 2026 on AI's role in marketing, alongside seven conference presentations across India. Running through all of it is a genuine interest in AI safety, interpretability, and responsible deployment — governance treated as part of the research problem, not an afterthought.

Before returning to academia full-time, he spent two years in professional practice: as a Process Associate handling insurance and financial workflows at Gallagher Service Center, and earlier as an Audit Assistant at a chartered accountancy firm — grounding his data instincts in real financial systems before turning them toward AI research.

UGC-NET · Commerce UGC-NET · Management Kerala SET · Commerce Best Paper — REVA 2024 Scopus Q1 Author

"The interesting question isn't just what a model predicts — it's whether we understand why, and whether we should trust it."
